page: Microsoft Azure F2as_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. It provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs with a single thread per core configuration. The cache layout comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, as well as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions. System memory totals 8.0 GB, allocating 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes no local storage, relying on external network-attached volumes, and includes no GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded processing capabilities, reaching a Geekbench single-core score of 2056.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3080.07, both ranking in the upper quartile. However, the limited 2-vCPU configuration constrains overall multithreaded capacity, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 3781.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 5382.71 falling into lower quartiles. Memory bandwidth yields 38.2 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 28.17 GB/sec for writes. Workload tests show a static web serving throughput of 4.22 GB/sec and Redis SET performance of 5.34 million operations per second, while small-model (135M) LLM inference processes 573.44 prompt tokens per second and generates 167.15 tokens per second.

Given its high core clock frequency and modern vector instruction set, the F2as_v6 offers efficient resource density for single-threaded processing tasks and smaller compute workloads without the overhead of larger core counts. The absence of local disk requires external persistent storage provisioning, which introduces network I/O considerations. This virtual machine is best suited for lightweight web application serving, batch processing tasks with low parallelism, microservices, and modest single-threaded computational tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure F2as_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine driven by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 8.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core), it incorporates AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic hardware acceleration. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier single-core compute performance, as reflected in high Geekbench and stress-ng single-threaded scores, balanced by moderate multi-core throughput typical of a dual-core machine. Memory throughput reaches 38.2 GB/sec on uncached reads and 28.17 GB/sec on writes, alongside moderate lightweight LLM token generation rates. The F2as_v6 is engineered for latency-sensitive single-threaded tasks, microservices, background jobs, and lightweight web serving workloads requiring high per-core execution speeds without large-scale parallelization.
